articles.title: El Bayern aborda el futuro de Musiala tras la polémica por su contrato y sus problemas neurológicos
articles.standfirst: El club alemán se ha reunido con los representantes del futbolista para aclarar su situación tras las declaraciones de Rummenigge y la reacción de FIFPro
articles.summary: El club alemán se ha reunido con los representantes del futbolista para aclarar su situación tras las declaraciones de Rummenigge y la reacción de FIFPro
articles.body: Jamal Musiala vive una etapa complicada en su carrera. El jugador del Bayern de Múnich, de 23 años, ha sufrido un nuevo episodio relacionado con la disfunción neurológica que le diagnosticaron el pasado verano. Una situación que ha vuelto a encender las alarmas sobre su estado de salud y que coincide con la polémica surgida alrededor de su contrato. El alemán renovó en febrero de 2025 hasta 2030, pero las recientes declaraciones de algunos dirigentes del Bayern han abierto el debate sobre una posible revisión de sus condiciones económicas. Ante el revuelo generado, el club confirmó que se reunió con los representantes del futbolista para abordar la situación. En su comunicado, la entidad bávara quiso dejar claro que la recuperación está por encima de cualquier otra cuestión: “La salud del jugador está por encima de todo para ambas partes. Jamal Musiala cuenta con todo el apoyo en su proceso de recuperación”. Además, explicó que los primeros síntomas neurológicos se detectaron el 22 de abril de 2025 y fueron evaluados junto al equipo médico del club. La polémica aumentó después de las declaraciones de Karl-Heinz Rummenigge a 'Sky', en las que planteó la necesidad de revisar las condiciones económicas del contrato si la situación deportiva del jugador no evoluciona como esperan. "Necesitamos hablar con la familia, el jugador y, sobre todo, con la agencia. Porque esas sumas, con todo respeto, ya no son viables", afirmó. No obstante, descartó una posible salida del futbolista: "No me imagino a Jamal dejando el club ni a otro club comprándolo en estas circunstancias". Sus palabras provocaron la reacción de FIFPro, que cuestionó públicamente la postura del Bayern y acusó al club de intentar presionar al jugador y a sus representantes de cara a futuras negociaciones. "Los contratos están para respetarse. Una lesión o un bajón de forma no dan derecho a un club a renegociar las condiciones que acordó", defendió el sindicato de futbolistas, que considera que cualquier preocupación contractual debería tratarse de manera privada. En el entorno de Musiala, como contó MARCA, molestaron estas palabras y, sobre todo, que éstas hayan alimentado el bulo en redes de que el jugador se puede retirar. Por ahora, la situación es clara: Jamal reapareció el pasado viernes ante el Colonia y la idea es convivir -mientras se trata, obviamente- con la deficiencia neurológica. Ayer martes tuvo lugar una conversación constructiva entre el FC Bayern München y los representantes de Jamal Musiala. La salud del jugador está por encima de todo para ambas partes. Musiala cuenta con todo el apoyo en su proceso de recuperación. Ante los numerosos rumores surgidos en los últimos días, el FC Bayern y 11WINS, la agencia que representa a Jamal, aclaran lo siguiente: Jamal Musiala fue examinado por primera vez el 22 de abril de 2025 por síntomas similares a los de las crisis de ausencia. Esto se llevó a cabo en coordinación con el FC Bayern y su departamento médico, inmediatamente después de la primera aparición de los síntomas neurológicos. El FC Bayern y los representantes de Jamal Musiala han acordado continuar las conversaciones en un clima de colaboración y confidencialidad.

articles.title: Cucho regresa por la puerta grande
articles.standfirst: El delantero fue protagonista con dos goles en la victoria del Betis en Bratislava
articles.summary: El delantero fue protagonista con dos goles en la victoria del Betis en Bratislava
articles.body: Cucho Hernández fue la estrella en la noche de Champions del Betis en Bratislava. El colombiano reaparecía como titular tras superar la lesión en la zona del sóleo proximal izquierdo que sufrió a mediados del pasado mes de octubre en el partido frente al Barcelona. Y lo hizo marcando dos goles que dejan a su equipo virtualmente clasificado para el Top 24 de la competición. Dos cabezazos, con los goles correspondientes, que confirman al cafetero como el mejor delantero que tiene Manuel Pellegrini. Ayer alcanzó los 25 goles con el Betis, siendo además el primer colombiano que marca un doblete con un equipo español en la Copa de Europa y también es el máximo goleador del Betis en la Champions League igualando a Ricardo Oliveira con tres goles. "No soy alto para tener tan buenos números de cabeza, pero tengo el timing bastante entrenado y tengo ya varios goles", revelaba tras el partido. Pero no son goles lo único que aporta al Betis. Exhibición en 63 minutos. Visión de juego, desborde, pegada, pases al espacio... Para la retina, su apertura a Abde en una acción que también pudo ampliar la renta verdiblanca. El delantero se mostró ambicioso: "Es un paso grande para nosotros, pero nuestro techo está más allá. Con mucha ambición, y con los pies en el suelo, queremos pasar entre los ocho primeros". Cucho, según las palabras de Pellegrini, no jugó el derbi del pasado sábado porque fue amonestado en el banquillo a los diez minutos de partido y el Ingeniero prefirió no correr el riesgo en ningún momento de quedarse con uno menos. Sí lo alineó en Bratislava, para alegría de la afición verdiblanca y beneficio del equipo. "Venía recién recuperándose, no estaba para muchos minutos y me alegro que haya convertido los dos goles”, dijo el técnico tras el partido. Los goles de Cucho Hernández han asegurado virtualmente la clasificación para el Top 24 en la Champions y colocan al Betis en disposición de pelear como el que más por entrar en el Top 8. "El primer logro es que estamos clasificados, al menos virtualmente, pero quedan tres partidos, nueve puntos y no hay que ser conformistas", dijo Pellegrini. La ambición del Betis es una de sus virtudes y, con un jugador como el colombiano, todo es más fácil.

articles.title: Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw: Lincoln City sack joint head coaches
articles.summary: Lincoln sack head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw just six months after they took joint charge of the Championship side.
articles.body:
Lincoln City have sacked their head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw just six months after they took joint charge of the Championship side.

The pair departed a little over 12 hours after they oversaw a 4-0 defeat at fellow strugglers Charlton Athletic on Tuesday.

The loss leaves the Imps just three points above the relegation places in what is the club's first season back in the second tier for 65 years.

Cohen and Shaw were assistant coaches under Michael Skubala when Lincoln were promoted as League One title winners last season.

They were surprisingly promoted to replace their boss as a joint managerial double act.

The duo oversaw just four wins from 17 league games this season, and Tuesday's loss at The Valley was their fifth in succession and heaviest since being thumped 6-0 by West Ham in mid-October.

Lincoln's chairman Ron Fowler, the American billionaire who took a controlling stake in the club when they were on their way to promotion last season, said the decision to sack the pair was in the "best interests" of the Imps.

"We have worked incredibly hard to reach the Championship and will do everything in our power to retain our status in this division," he told the club website. , external

First-team coach Shaun Pearson will take charge of Lincoln, with the support of Paul McShane and David Preece, on an interim basis.

Lincoln are next in action on Saturday when they host high-flying Wolves.

articles.title: Why Ole Miss players look forward to ex-QB's emotional speech before every Egg Bowl
articles.summary: Former Ole Miss football quarterback Tom Luke has built a recent tradition of giving an Egg Bowl speech before the game
articles.body:
OXFORD − Star Ole Miss football defensive lineman Will Echoles has heard Tom Luke's Egg Bowl speech three times.

"I think every year he gets more and more fired up," Echoles said Nov. 24. "From my freshman year to now, it's always about a kid on the playground fight between Mississippi State and Ole Miss ."

No. 19 Ole Miss (7-4, 4-4 SEC) will host Mississippi State football (5-6, 2-6) in the Egg Bowl on Nov. 27 (11 a.m., ABC).

Luke's speech has become a tradition for Ole Miss. He gets up in front of the team the Sunday before the Egg Bowl to educate the new players on the game's importance. Coach Pete Golding described it as one of his favorite days of the year.

Luke's title is associate AD for player development. He is from Gulfport and played quarterback at Ole Miss for three seasons (1989-91) before suffering concussions that led to him deciding to forgo his senior season. He finished his career with 1,524 passing yards.

Luke went 2-1 in Egg Bowls and 1-1 as the starter. The Rebels won 21-11 in 1989, 21-9 in 1990 and lost 24-9 in 1991. All three of those games were in Jackson.

"It's intense," offensive tackle Terez Davis said. "Just from his time playing here, I think he's played in it three times and lost to them once. He hates (the loss). He kind of just expresses his feeling towards it. Just trying to motivate us to beat them."

Tight end Luke Hasz said Luke spoke about the pain of losing the game in 1991.

"He wishes he could do anything to get it back," Hasz said. "He just has a bunch of other stuff with the story that is really impactful and helps fire us up."

Ole Miss won the Egg Bowl 38-19 in Starkville in 2025 for its third straight win in the series. Echoles said he remembers how happy Luke was after the game, and it's infectious.

"Just to see him with a smile on his face after we won last year, how he carries himself and how much this game means to him," Echoles said.

What Will Echoles said about Ole Miss football bowl game status

Even without a win in the Egg Bowl, the Rebels have clinched bowl eligibility.

Because it's not a College Football Playoff game, high-profile Ole Miss players have more incentive to skip the game to avoid injury and prepare for the 2027 NFL Draft.

Echoles is one of those players. He's projected to be a first-round pick. He said he has not decided if he will play in the Rebels' bowl game. Hasz and Davis both committed to playing in it.

"I'm just taking it day-by-day, honestly," Echoles said. "I haven't talked with (Golding) about that, so we'll just take it day-by-day."

UCF football is going bowling once again! The Knights can head into the postseason with their best record since 2022 with a road win over sputtering Colorado .

The on-again, off-again offense turned all the way up in UCF's 48-17 win over Iowa State . Alonza Barnett III had easily his best game in Orlando with nearly 300 total yards to go with five touchdowns (four passing, one rushing). With Duke Watson back in the backfield, the Knights (6-5, 4-4 in Big 12) ran for 205 yards, their highest output since Sept. 19 against Georgia State.

The going has been much tougher for coach Deion Sanders and the Buffaloes, 4-7 (2-6) after last week's 35-28 loss at Cincinnati. Utah transfer Isaac Wilson threw for a career-high 312 yards and three touchdowns, but he added three interceptions, giving him 12 on the year. Joseph Williams, the Big 12's second-leading receiver, hauled in a 70-yard score to keep hope alive late in that game.

Guessing which UCF team will show up week to week is a difficult endeavor: They've averaged 40 points per game in three wins since their bye week Oct. 17 and 12 in two losses. Having Duke Watson, Taevion Swint and Landon Chambers in the lineup at the same time could help stabilize the offense, as well Alonza Barnett's growing rapport with standout receiver Josh Derry .

Colorado has played better at home, upsetting Houston on Nov. 13 and keeping undefeated Utah close throughout their meeting on Halloween. And though their offense ranks last in the Big 12 (22.5 points per game), we are a month removed from the Knights coughing up 41 in the Space Game to Baylor, the conference's third-worst offense. It's hard to trust UCF to take care of business, and before winning a thriller at Kansas earlier this month, they had lost 12 in a row away from the Bounce House.

articles.title: Wisconsin's Mason Posa named one of five finalists for Butkus Award
articles.summary: Wisconsin football linebacker Mason Posa has been named one of five finalists for the 2026 Butkus Award, which recognizes the nation's top linebacker.
articles.body:
Wisconsin Badgers football linebacker Mason Posa has been named one of five finalists for the 2026 Butkus Award, which recognizes the nation's top linebacker.

The sophomore has been a standout for the Badgers ' defense this season, recording 51 solo tackles, the most in the Big Ten. He also leads the nation with 54 Pro Football Focus stops, a statistic that measures tackles resulting in a negative outcome for the opposing offense.

Posa has recorded at least one tackle for loss in five of Wisconsin 's seven Big Ten games and was previously named a semifinalist for the Bednarik Award . He also earned Freshman All-American honors in 2025.

The Albuquerque, New Mexico, native is the first Wisconsin linebacker to reach the Butkus Award finalist stage since Leo Chenal in 2021. Zack Baun (2019) and T.J. Edwards (2017) are the other Badgers to earn finalist recognition in recent years.

Posa joins Texas' Rasheem Biles, Georgia's Chris Cole, UCLA's Sammy Omosigho and Texas Tech's Bren Roberts as one of five finalists. The winner is expected to be announced the week of Dec. 7.

Wisconsin has yet to have a player win the award , giving Posa an opportunity to make program history.

The Miami Hurricanes close out the regular season not having to worry about a slip-up against Boston College costing them a spot in the ACC championship game . But if they're not careful, their all-but-guaranteed spot in the College Football Playoff could come into question.

Miami (10-1, 8-0 in ACC) secured its place in Charlotte with a 28-20 win over Virginia Tech . Mark Fletcher Jr. ran for 63 yards and all three of the Canes' touchdowns, while Darian Mensah doubled his interception total for the year (from two all the way up to four). The quarterback made due with not only fellow Heisman hopeful Malachi Toney out for the third straight game, but with tight end Elija Lofton missing most of the game as well.

BC can't be counted out: At 5-6 (3-4), Bill O'Brien and the Eagles are one win shy of bowl eligibility. They snapped a three-game losing skid by beating Syracuse 27-15 on Senior Day, with running back Bo McCormack III exploding for 236 yards and a touchdown. The sophomore tacked on five catches for 45 yards, also a career high, while Mason McKenzie passed for two scores.

Miami Hurricanes football vs Virginia Tech: Photos from ACC game

Miami football schedule: Hurricanes' next game

Miami, ranked No. 4 in the US LBM Coaches Poll , hosts Boston College on Saturday in their Week 13 game. The game will air on ESPN with streaming options including Fubo , which offers a free trial for new subscribers.

As of 2 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 24, tickets to Miami-BC were available for as low as $17 with seats in the lower bowl going for $61. To see a full list of ticket prices, visit StubHub .

The Hurricanes and Eagles kick off at noon on Saturday at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida.

Since Malachi Toney went down with a high ankle sprain, Miami's three games have followed similar scripts: lethargic starts that give way to a more familiar all-gears-clicking offense in the second half. It would make all Canes fans relieved if they broke that trend against BC's middling defense, ranked 14th of 17 ACC team in scoring (27.2 points per game) and 12th in yardage (375 per game). The potential return of starting guard Max Buchanan, out since the Clemson game Oct. 3, could help on that front.

Syracuse is the only FBS team to score fewer than 21 points against the Eagles this season, and over their preceding three-game slide, BC gave up nearly 40 points per game. That's not great news when you're about to go up against the offense that's led the nation in scoring for most of the year (Miami is all the way down to No. 2 with Toney on the mend, but they're still putting up almost 30 ppg over that stretch).

It's also not a good sign that a faltering UM offense remains BC's best path to an upset. The Eagles do have a strong run game with Mason McKenzie and Bo McCormack both top-10 rushers in the ACC (718 and 638 yards, respectively), but Miami's No. 1 rushing defense (68.1 ypg) just survived Nate Sheppard two weeks ago. McCormack repeating his outburst seems unlikely, and McKenzie rates worse as a passer than Walker Eget; BC is dead last in the ACC with 168.4 passing yards per game.

It's also not a good sign that a faltering UM offense remains BC's best path to an upset. The Eagles do have a strong run game with Mason McKenzie and Bo McCormack both top-10 rushers in the ACC (718 and 638 yards, respectively), but Miami's No. 1 rushing defense (68.1 ypg) just survived Nate Sheppard two weeks ago. McCormack repeating his outburst seems unlikely, and McKenzie rates worse as a passer than Walker Eget; BC is dead last in the ACC with 168.4 passing yards per game.

articles.title: Jobe Bellingham names Arsenal star as tactical weak link as Borussia Dortmund man reveals ruthless Champions League plan
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham has shed light on the tactical instructions that helped his side frustrate Arsenal in their Champions League enc...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham has shed light on the tactical instructions that helped his side frustrate Arsenal in their Champions League encounter. The 21-year-old explained how BVB coaches identified a specific physical vulnerability in the Gunners' backline to swing the momentum in London.

Dortmund fight back after early Arsenal dominance

Arsenal dominated the opening half in London and led through Viktor Gyokeres' spectacular early strike. Despite creating enough chances to put the contest out of reach before the interval, the hosts held only a narrow advantage at the break.

The Bundesliga leaders emerged transformed for the second period, adopting a physical, man-to-man approach that gradually wrested control from the Gunners. Maximilian Beier rewarded that resurgence with a deserved equaliser.

Dortmund came millimetres from snatching victory when Bellingham finished from close range, only for an offside flag to rule it out. Both the 21-year-old and Myles Lewis-Skelly, whom he had targeted, were substituted shortly afterwards.

Bellingham details coaching plan to target Lewis-Skelly

Speaking to Amazon Prime Video , Bellingham credited Dortmund's coaching staff for spotting a key aerial matchup against Lewis-Skelly. He noted that facing the Arsenal player offered a clearer route up the pitch than battling more imposing defenders.

"One of the coaches pointed out to me that I was against Myles [Lewis-Skelly]," he explained. "For the long ball - I don't want to say a mismatch - but I'm obviously bigger. You would expect that if I was against Gabriel or Ezri [Konsa] it would be a bit more difficult to win the long balls."

Bellingham added that using his frame helped relieve pressure: "I thought that there was a bit of an advantage there in terms of height. I managed to win a few flick-ons and get us up the pitch."

Tactical variety and narrow margins define Dortmund's display

Going direct was only part of Dortmund's turnaround, as they paired aerial duels with sharper ball retention and tighter defensive organisation. Bellingham praised how well his side adapted across every phase to earn a point.

"We varied it well, we played short, and we retained possession and defended a lot better in transitions," the midfielder said.

Having come close to marking his return to English soil with a late winner, he admitted the offside decision stung: "Gutted. A bit unlucky at the minute. It would have been nice if it was today, back in England."

Bundesliga leaders look to build on London resilience

Leaving London with a valuable Champions League point reinforces the momentum Borussia Dortmund have built atop the Bundesliga. Withstanding heavy early pressure and adapting mid-game against elite opposition gives the German side a proven tactical blueprint.

For Bellingham, the focus now turns to converting strong displays into decisive moments in front of goal. After seeing a close-range strike ruled out by millimetres, the 21-year-old will hope fortune favours him as Dortmund's campaign continues.

articles.title: Moving the chains: Female tackle football player flourishes on the field

articles.body:
The Indiana Valor offense huddled up during a practice at Greenwood Fieldhouse. With her glasses slipping slightly off her nose and an American flag mouthguard in place, center Bonnie Huckeby led the women's professional tackle football team through its next play, snapping the ball to her quarterback.

The 30-year-old has spent her entire life leading and helping others. As a former softball player and coach, powerlifter and dedicated community member, being named a captain in her first year with the Valor felt like a natural fit.

"I lead from beside, not from in front of or behind," she said. "I'm going to go through the trenches with you. Like, we're going to get through it together."

Huckeby joined the team during the 2026 season, and became a starter and playing every offensive snap in game action. But training hasn't been easy as a mom, a wife and a full-time employee in hospice care.

The team practices twice a week during the season, and Huckeby does two to three additional workouts a week when she can find the time.

See Indy women's professional tackle football team's starting center in action

"I really don't have a schedule," she said. "It's when can I fit this workout in? Is it going to be at home? Is it going to be at the gym? Obviously, things are chaotic, but I still make it happen."

Amid the chaos, Huckeby said she and her teammates are extremely supportive of one another because they share daily obstacles of motherhood and being an athlete.

"I don't think there's anybody better for the sport of football than a mom, especially for offense," she said. "We sacrifice ourselves all for the better of our team. That's what a mom does. You're sacrificing yourself, your body, everything that you do for your children. So, it just comes naturally."

With her team alongside her, Huckeby is excited for the future of women's professional football and hopes the league and its players continue to grow and gain respect.

"You should have a full respect for a woman who works 40 hours a week, and is also a mom, and they're also playing professional football on the weekends," she said. "I don't know why anybody wouldn't want to pay to see that.

articles.title: Group of Six power rankings: Does Boise State loss open door for another CFP contender?
articles.summary: Here are our latest Group of Six power rankings after Boise State's upset loss in Week 12:
articles.body:
Boise State clinched a Pac-12 championship game berth against San Diego State, although its loss to the Aztecs in Week 12 could potentially shake up the Group of Six race for the final College Football Playoff berth.

The Broncos were shocked by San Diego State 22-20 in Week 12, setting up a rematch between the two teams for a conference championship on Dec. 4. Boise State was the highest-ranked non-Power Four team entering Week 12, but with the same number of losses of American frontrunner UTSA or even 10-1 Liberty, perhaps there will be some intrigue around the Group of Six race down the stretch.

The five highest-ranked conference champions earn an automatic berth to the CFP each year. With potential upsets in conference championship games across the country, there could be some chaos in terms of which team lands the final CFP spot.

Each week, USA TODAY Sports ranks the best Group of Six teams. Here are our latest power rankings after Week 12:

Group of Six power rankings after Week 12

Maddux Madsen had his worst game of the season against San Diego State, throwing two interceptions and fumbling once in the 22-20 loss. The Broncos put up 412 total yards, but their turnovers were the difference in the game.

San Diego State's win knocked Texas State out of the Pac-12 championship game, forcing a rematch against Boise State. Boise State is still the frontrunner for a CFP berth among Group of Six teams but can't slip up the next two weeks against Colorado State or San Diego State.

New Mexico bounce back from its 21-17 loss to UNLV in Week 11 by defeating Wyoming 24-17 on the road in a tough environment. The Lobos can clinch a spot in the Mountain West championship game with a win over Air Force in their season finale, with North Dakota State, Wyoming, Air Force and UNLV all still in contention for the title game.

A win would give New Mexico a 10-2 finish with one loss in conference play and its other loss a close 14-6 game against Oklahoma on the road. Its resume is solid, but might need some help for a CFP bid.

UTSA escaped UAB with a 19-17 win in a gross second half, where the Roadrunners outscored the Blazers 5-3 after being tied 14-14 at halftime.

Coach Jeff Traylor's candidacy at Baylor is heating up, but UTSA can clinch a spot in the American championship game with a win over Tulsa in Week 13. Win out, and the Roadrunners have a real case over Boise State for the final CFP berth.

Liberty keeps destroying everyone in Conference USA, which is probably the worst conference in college football. Still, it's up to a whopping No. 17 in ESPN's SP+ metric and is amid a 10-game win streak after losing to James Madison in the season opener.

Liberty ends its season against Missouri State and Jacksonville State in the CUSA championship game, but is making a case for a CFP bid after moving into the US LBM Coaches Poll for the first time this season.

Louisiana Tech has probably been underrated a bit too much this season, with its only two losses being against LSU and Baylor, two teams it was competitive against for large portions of the game.

The Bulldogs have won eight consecutive games since losing those back-to-back nonconference games with an undefeated Sun Belt record. Quarterback Blake Baker has a 21-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio, and tight end Eli Finley was named a finalist for the Mackey Award as he leads the nation in receiving yards among tight ends with 709 receiving yards this season.

Louisiana Tech ends its season against Georgia Southern, which it could rematch again in the conference championship game next week.

Memphis was in the driver's seat for an American championship game berth, but its loss to Navy in Week 12 threw in a wrench in those plans. The Tigers can still play themselves into the game, but the upset loss was certainly game changing.

Memphis committed three turnovers in the 38-34 loss and allowed 335 rushing yards and 6.2 yards per carry against the Midshipmen. First-year coach Charles Huff announced Nov. 24 he's returning for next season, giving the program some momentum into 2027, but blowing a 10-point lead against Navy and potentially also an American championship game berth hurts.

Honorable mentions: North Dakota State, San Diego State, Air Force, North Texas

articles.title: Zidane was much better than me: Bellingham after Real Madrid wonder goal
articles.summary: Jude Bellingham admits he had ‘no idea’ what he’d done after scoring a goal that drew comparisons with Zinedine Zidane.
articles.body:
Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham has brushed aside comparisons with football great Zinedine Zidane following his sensational goal against PSV in the Champions League.

The England international came on at half-time with Los Blancos trailing and inspired a sensational second-half display, including a magnificent effort from distance, at the Santiago Bernabeu on Tuesday.

Bellingham said he “did not know” how he scored his brilliant goal, flicking the ball up on the edge of the box and slicing a stunning effort inside the far post.

Having seen an acrobatic volley blocked minutes earlier, the England midfielder controlled Kylian Mbappe’s pass with two touches in the air and curled a superb shot into ⁠⁠the far corner from well outside the area.

“I have no idea what I did,” Bellingham told RMTV. “I had the ball in a good position and thought about shooting.”

The 23-year-old, upon joining Real Madrid, took Zidane’s number five shirt in “homage” to the Frenchman, whom he admired, and some have compared his goal to a Zidane-style strike.

“I do things that you guys think are similar to Zidane, but he was much better than me,” Bellingham told reporters.

Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho hailed Bellingham’s game-changing display as the midfielder gave Mourinho credit for helping him find arguably the best form he has enjoyed at Madrid in recent weeks, with Los Blancos winning a 10th straight match, but the coach said the midfielder only had himself to thank.

“I think the main figure responsible for what Jude is today is Jude, and his teammates. I try to help a little,” said the Portuguese coach.

“He’s an absolutely extraordinary player who has everything – he has physicality, he has technique, he has tactical understanding of the game, he has ambition, he has absolutely everything and today, obviously not by himself, but he changed the direction of the match.”

“He’s an absolutely extraordinary player and for me, without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world,” Mourinho said.

Madrid’s victory over the Dutch champions maintained their 100 percent start to the league phase, in which they are provisional leaders.

Mourinho reiterated his view that it was a “scandal” that Bellingham was not ranked in the top 10 players in the world at this year’s Ballon d’Or ceremony.

Mbappe netted twice to put Real out of sight before Vinicius Jr got in on the act with a late goal, having struck the post twice earlier in the game.

articles.title: Raheem Sterling: Former England international given suspended 12-month jail sentence for dangerous driving
articles.summary: Raheem Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September and admitted possession of six nitrous oxide cannisters for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen
articles.body:
Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on May 28. The sentence is suspended for 18 months.

He has also been handed a two-year driving ban and must undertake 100 hours of unpaid community work. Sterling will have to re-take a driving test to hold a licence.

The 31-year-old admitted possession of six nitrous oxide cannisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Mitigating factors taken into account by District Judge Kirsty Allman were Sterling's guilty plea, that he had no prior convictions and a clean driving licence prior to his arrest in May.

She also said she took into account Sterling's regret at his behaviour, attached great weight to testimonies about his character and the fact that, away from his footballing career and perhaps not in the public sphere, he is heavily involved with several charitable causes from the Raheem Sterling Foundation, the RS7 Academy and several charitable bursaries.

Further mitigation was that Sterling engaged with addiction services soon after his arrest in May and admitted himself into residential care for 12 days at an addiction centre, which the court saw as "genuine engagement".

The judge said Sterling was entirely culpable for the dangerous driving charge, saying: "You chose to drive, disregarding the safety of others".

Chief Inspector Chris Sharland from Hampshire Police said: "Nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas or NOS, is a Class C drug, and driving whilst under its influence is an emerging threat to the safety of motorists on our roads.

"Driving whilst impaired with nitrous oxide can cause unconsciousness, and in the worst-case scenarios neurological damage or death, so there is a very real risk of causing serious harm to yourself or other motorists.

"We urge drivers to be aware of not only the law, but the risk this type of behaviour carries - one decision can have devastating consequences."

Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate's side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020. He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019. He left for Chelsea in 2022 but after falling out of favour spent the 2024/25 season on loan at Arsenal.

Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the 2025/26 season. He is currently without a club.

In the 2021 Queen's Birthday Honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out strongly against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.

Sky Sports News' Geraint Hughes at Basingstoke Magistrates Court:

"When Raheem Sterling arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates Court for his sentencing, as you would expect he looked serious, but also quite anxious.

"He was wearing dark clothing and never once did his gaze do anything other than look forward or towards the judge inside the courtroom. You felt he was aware of the gravity of the situation and also - given that his legal team had told the court how ashamed he felt to be in this position and that he never ever wanted to be in front of a criminal court in his life again - you could sense that with his body language and his demeanour.

"When the district judge asked Raheem Sterling to stand while she delivered her sentence he did so at times looking downwards, but mainly straight at the judge, occasionally acknowledging her remarks.

"At the conclusion of her sentencing, when Sterling was told he was free to leave the court, there was no smile or any emotion. He just walked out of the courtroom with his legal team to whom he shook their hands and thanked them very quietly before being able to leave the court a free man having avoided a potential custodial sentence."

articles.title: Raheem Sterling enjoyed a wonderful Premier League career but regularly attracted controversy - is there any way back?
articles.summary: Is there any way back to the top level in professional football for Raheem Sterling after he was handed a suspended 12-month prison sentence? Laura Hunter and Ben Ransom look at a career that hit the heights with Man City and England, but now finds Sterling without a club at just 31
articles.body:
Sterling played a dominant role in Manchester City's most definitive era, one led by the greatest tactical mind of a generation. But this forward exuded genius of his own.

A teenage prodigy that climbed his way to the very top of the game, Sterling was driven by his origin story rather than burdened by it. At his height, he drew comparisons to Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo as a player capable of "winning the race", according to Barcelona great Xavi, to become the world's next best thing.

His 82 international caps pointed towards a boundless trajectory; England's most impactful player on their run to the Euro 2020 final. In an alternate world, he would still be part of Thomas Tuchel's England set-up now, the coach being a key advocate for the move that took Sterling from Man City to Chelsea in 2022. He was still only 27.

For a player that burst onto the scene an entire decade before, Sterling's status and authority at the top was enduring. He made his Liverpool debut at 17 and his senior England bow 24 days before his 18th birthday. The peak of his Premier League powers ran parallel with many of the game's elite performers. That should not be forgotten.

And yet, the cut and thrust of the limelight, however perpetual, had consequences. Its punishing effects are all that seem to remain of a career fatigued by comebacks. Perhaps this particular juncture, one that has seen Sterling receive a suspended sentence for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide, is one return too many.

Throughout the now-31-year-old's on-field journey there were many flashpoints of tension. From his acrimonious Liverpool exit to his eventual exile at Chelsea, Sterling was poured over: talked about, written about, dissected and scrutinised from one performance to the next. That is the reality of a modern-day footballer.

He divided public sentiment throughout that time but almost always used the immensity of his talent to wage war on the pitch, continuing to produce when it really mattered.

Sterling rejected his characterisation of a "money-grabbing 20-year-old" before leaving Liverpool in 2015. His time at Man City yielded four league titles, including a domestic treble where he was championed as "Wembley boy" after scoring twice in the FA Cup final. A full circle moment for the kid who had grown up in nearby Neasden watching the new stadium being built.

"One reason why we are here is Raheem," raved Pep Guardiola. Sky Sports' City reporter Ben Ransom remembers his contribution equally fondly: "His dribbling electrified the Etihad and 'typical City' at that time was a flowing move finished by Sterling. The title-winning sides of 2018 and 2019 were the best teams I've ever seen in the Premier League."

Earlier in his international career, Sterling's setbacks also played out in the public domain. There was a run-in with Roy Hodgson over being "too tired" to play, before being a principal scapegoat for England's Euro 2016 exit. Despite becoming increasingly prolific for Man City, Sterling went 27 international appearances without scoring. After a tirade of online abuse, some of it racially motivated, he labelled himself #TheHatedOne.

But the script flipped spectacularly in October 2018 in a 3-2 win over Spain and he grew to become decisive at the next major tournament in 2021; England's most reliable creative source. Once again doubters were silenced. Critics caged until the next episode, which of course was destined to surface before long. This is Raheem Sterling.

Towards the end of his time at City he had lost his starting place but the passion to compete still burned. To start again seemed sensible. But leaving the structure of a club steeped in recent success for a Chelsea side thrown into chaos by the Clearlake-Todd Boehly takeover was unlikely to offer much solace. Besides, Sterling's output was already stalling.

A line from his first Chelsea address to reporters sticks in the mind.

"I felt my game time at Man City was getting limited for different reasons and I couldn't afford to waste more time," he said in August 2022. "When I look back in the future, I never wanted to see a rise then a decline." The sense of foreboding is hard to overlook.

Another challenge of the modern-day superstar, one that soars to fame in their teenage years, is physical toll. The deterioration of a player so reliant on speed and burst for goals was perhaps always going to happen. The only question was when. "City were built with a blend of technical brilliance, fluidity and speed. On the pitch Sterling excelled in all of those areas," Ransom remembers. But pace can be both a blessing and, latterly, a curse.

Sterling had reached 500 career appearances by the age of 26. He has played 157 times since then; wear and tear an inevitable byproduct of so many minutes. Even Mikel Arteta, who worked closely with Sterling at City, could not reawaken his spark.

His loan period at Arsenal was meant to liberate a player scorned by Chelsea's churn but ended with one solitary strike in a Carabao Cup meeting with Bolton; which looks to be his final career goal. The less said about his ill-fated stretch at Feyenoord the better.

Of course Sterling was not just a victim of his tiring legs. Reports suggest his conduct at Chelsea was not always exemplary - clearly a frustrated figure forced to train alone but one that no longer set the standards of a professional at the very top of his game.

It will be characterised as the beginning of the end for a player that posted double figures in every single campaign while at City. One might also question whether Chelsea's treatment of him was just, too.

Sterling's career reaching its nadir at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court feels sad. Many will tell the tale of the rise and fall of one of the Premier League's best. Really, the narrative should reflect an individual whose impact was immense in the face of adversity and who used his platform for good during the peak years.

Ransom tells the story of a figure that "arguably made an even bigger impact off the pitch, publicly pointing out blatant hypocrisy and challenging stereotypes of Black athletes. Sterling didn't just speak up, he took on one of the most powerful newspaper editors in the country. He was a difference maker in every way." The Queen awarded him an MBE in 2021.

Whether Sterling was misaligned or misguided - or both - is up for interpretation. Whatever the judgement, he should not be pardoned for his recent trespasses. But nor should his many achievements be reduced to nothing.

articles.title: Sterling, condenado a 12 meses de cárcel por conducción temeraria drogado en un Lamborghini
articles.standfirst: El futbolista de 31 años se había declarado culpable previamente y admitió la posesión de óxido nitroso
articles.summary: El futbolista de 31 años se había declarado culpable previamente y admitió la posesión de óxido nitroso
articles.body: Raheem Sterling ha sido condenado por un episodio de conducción temeraria que protagonizó al volante de su Lamborghini en varias carreteras de Inglaterra. El jugador, de 31 años, reconoció los hechos y evita entrar en prisión al recibir una pena de 12 meses de cárcel suspendida durante 18 meses. La sentencia también incluye 100 horas de trabajos comunitarios y la retirada del permiso de conducir durante dos años. Sterling había admitido previamente haber circulado de manera peligrosa por la M25, la M3, la A327 y Minley Road, en Hampshire, antes de sufrir un accidente el pasado 28 de mayo. Además, el inglés reconoció la posesión de seis bombonas de óxido nitroso para su consumo ilegal y haberse negado a facilitar una muestra a la policía. Durante la vista celebrada en el Tribunal de Magistrados de Basingstoke, la jueza Kirsty Allman describió al futbolista como una persona de "buena reputación" y destacó que "su carácter ha sido ejemplar". Sterling, que ha vestido las camisetas de Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea y Arsenal y que ahora está sin equipo, no mostró ninguna reacción durante la lectura de la sentencia.

articles.title: Soccer Star Sterling Gets Suspended Jail Sentence for Dangerous Driving While Inhaling From Balloon
articles.summary: BASINGSTOKE, England (AP) — Former England soccer player Raheem Sterling was handed a suspended 12-month jail sentence on Wednesday after admitting to driving dangerously while inhaling from a balloon on a highway before being involved in a collision.
articles.body:
BASINGSTOKE, England (AP) — Former England soccer player Raheem Sterling was handed a suspended 12-month jail sentence on Wednesday after admitting to driving dangerously while inhaling from a balloon on a highway before being involved in a collision.

Sterling, 31, gave no reaction as the sentence was passed at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in relation to an incident on May 28 when he crashed his Lamborghini Urus on the M3 in southern England.

The sentence is suspended for 18 months.

He pleaded guilty on Sept. 15 to dangerous driving, possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Sterling also has been ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.

Police footage of Sterling's arrest on the day of the incident shows him in the crashed car with two canisters on his lap, as the officer tells him: "You can put that down, mate," Britain's Press Association reported.

His vehicle had veered off the carriageway and struck a metal gate during morning rush hour, causing damage to his car, the court heard. Officials previously said no other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported.

Sterling had been awake all night and was spotted at a fast-food restaurant at around 1 a.m. — more than seven hours before the collision — driving and taking nitrous oxide, the court heard.

District judge Kirsty Allman said Sterling exposed a "large number of road users to a significant risk of serious harm by the manner of your driving on two motorways and in peak travel time that morning," the Press Association reported.

The judge acknowledged that nitrous oxide had become a "maladaptive coping mechanism" for Sterling during a "difficult period" in his career.

"Importantly, shortly after your arrest and entirely voluntarily, you engaged with addiction services," she added.

Sterling, who scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, is currently without a club. He has played for a number of England's top teams — Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea and Arsenal — and was at Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal last season.

articles.title: Osmajic, del Cádiz a 'gladiador del gol' con De Rossi: "Es como esos perros grandes que se te echan encima"
articles.standfirst: El '9' del Genoa suma seis goles en la Serie A después de un paso gris por LaLiga
articles.summary: El '9' del Genoa suma seis goles en la Serie A después de un paso gris por LaLiga
articles.body: Milutin Osmajić (Podgorica, Montenegro; 1999) pasó por el Cádiz con más pena que gloria. Apenas consiguió marcar un gol en los 14 partidos (342') que disputó con el primer equipo. Los ocho tantos que marcó en su cesión al Vizela le valieron para marcharse traspasado al Preston NE a cambio de 2,5 millones de euros. En la Segunda inglesa terminó de explotar con un total de 31 dianas y seis asistencias en 111 envites. Cifras que este verano llevaron al Genoa a pagar otros 2,5 kilos por su traspaso. "La operación surgió porque Diego López lo vio junto con los ojeadores del club y enseguida nos enamoramos de sus cualidades", explica Daniele de Rossi. Sin embargo, el ex de la Roma, ahora entrenador del Genoa, no lo terminaba de ver: "En la lista había jugadores más prestigiosos, así que decidimos esperar. Cuando vimos que no estaban a nuestro alcance, no tuvimos dudas: era el mejor de los que podíamos fichar. Es cierto que he tenido suerte porque, pensándolo bien, quizá hubiera preferido a algún otro jugador más experimentado en la Serie A". El propio Osmajic, sobre el 'verde', se ha encargado de cargarle de razones. Sus seis goles en 11 partidos de Liga -suma también una asistencia- le sitúan como el quinto máximo anotador de la Serie A. Sobre todo, está demostrando una eficacia bárbara: el 28,6% de sus remates acaban en gol. De ahí que haya marcado más tantos (6) de los 3,88 que indica su índice de Goles Esperados (xG). Goles que valen su peso en oro para el Genoa, que se ha situado décimo con seis puntos, ocho por encima del descenso, después de encadenar cuatro victorias en las últimas cinco jornadas frente a Juventus (2-0), Sassuolo (0-2), Lecce (1-2) y Venezia (1-0). "Ha marcado seis goles, son números importantes. Es intenso, va a toda velocidad, incluso cuando tiene que abrazarte. ¿Has visto a esos perros grandes que se te echan encima para celebrar? Él es igual. Es muy fuerte. Es el jugador perfecto para nosotros", insiste De Rossi elogiando, también su 'otro' fútbol. Osmajic, que venía de marcar en el parón con Montenegro, se ha convertido en el 'gladiador del gol' de De Rossi: es el undécimo delantero de la Serie A que más faltas recibe (17). "Estoy contento con el míster. Nos da muchos consejos. Quiere que todos demos el 100 %. Estamos en el camino correcto". El ex del Cádiz pone al grupo por encima de sus propios intereses. "No debemos detenernos", asegura al tiempo que evita fijarse una cifra de goles: "No quiero hablar de eso. Prefiero centrarme en ayudar a mi equipo. Los goles llegarán". Al 'gladiador' del Genoa no hay quien le tumbe.

articles.title: David Affengruber masterclass against Erling Haaland showed why man-to-man marking is popular in Premier League
articles.summary: Manchester United's defensive mishap in their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool sparked a debate about man-to-man marking. But David Affengruber's performance against Erling Haaland in Fulham's draw against Manchester City showed why teams do it, writes Adam Bate...
articles.body:
There was a time when Leny Yoro might have been there to sweep up behind him. But Florian Wirtz was his priority, not covering for his colleague. Jamie Carragher's excellent analysis on Monday Night Football discussed this key tactical shift of recent years.

"This is a theme of the game now and also young defenders coming into it, they are obsessed with men and they do not understand the nuts and bolts of defending and the positions that they should be in," explained Carragher, speaking on Sky Sports .

The former Liverpool defender highlighted numerous examples from over the weekend. "It is probably different from when we played. The modern way of thinking is, 'he is my man and that is your man'. There is none of this zonal where you help each other."

But there was one perfect example - and, therefore, explanation - of why teams adopt this system. It came one day before Manchester United's unravelling at Anfield back in their own home city as Fulham's ambitious approach paid off away to Manchester City .

David Affengruber was left isolated up against Erling Haaland for much of the game. His central-defensive partner Calvin Bassey tracked Phil Foden deep into opposition territory, which, on the face of it, left the Austria international in a vulnerable position.

Haaland has a four-inch height advantage on Affengruber and boasts a huge frame with which to protect the ball. The defender might have been overwhelmed but through canny body positioning was able to deliver a masterclass in one-against-one defending.

The City fans became increasingly frustrated by Haaland's inability to make the ball stick. The striker finished the game having completed fewer than half of his passes for the first time this season. It was largely due to the constant attentions of his marker.

But Affengruber's performance did more than just prove that a man-to-man system could stop even the best out-and-out striker on the planet. It gave his Fulham side the platform from which they were able to earn a deserved 1-1 draw at the Etihad Stadium.

Speaking to Alvaro Arbeloa afterwards, it was an opportunity to ask why it was that the Fulham coach had taken this brave move to trust his defender to deal with Haaland. This was not some sado-masochistic assignment. It was done for a specific purpose.

"For me, as a manager, if you want to be aggressive, if you want to press high, in the last line you cannot defend with one more player," explained the former Real Madrid head coach. "You can defend with one more player in other lines but not in the last one."

Arbeloa added: "Obviously, there are many players who know how to defend really aggressive, and press really aggressive, with two centre-backs against Haaland. For me, the best way to defend is aggressive, it is man-to-man in the last line."

The reason is that by going man-to-man Fulham ensured that the City side did not have a numerical advantage elsewhere. "I felt that we could press them really well if we go man-to-man. And David and Calvin, especially David, did really well against Erling."

This commitment to pressing high gave Fulham a foothold. They had 45 per cent of the possession in the first half with a passing accuracy of almost 87 per cent. That is the highest of any visiting team against Manchester City in the Premier League so far this season.

The man-to-man system enabled Fulham's forwards to lock on to an opponent and impose enough of their game on City to cause Enzo Maresca's team problems from the start. It made for an enjoyable game - and an enjoyable away day for the travelling fans.

Whether Affengruber enjoyed his tightrope walk of an afternoon quite so much is unclear. There is no doubt that the 25-year-old summer signing from Elche would have been in Arbeloa's thoughts when praising the courage of his players. He facilitated it all.

And, in stark contrast to De Ligt at Anfield, Affengruber showed what was possible when a defender wins their individual duel with the striker. Man-to-man marking is a risky business. But when it can work even up against Haaland, the rewards are there too.

articles.title: Afcon 2025 final Cas verdict: Senegal hail 'justice for sport' but Morocco left unsatisfied
articles.summary: Players and officials in Senegal have welcomed the decision to reinstate the West Africans as Afcon 2025 champions, but those in Morocco still contest the decision.
articles.body:
That was the initial reaction of Senegal football federation (FSF) president Abdoulaye Fall to the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to reinstate the West Africans as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions.

The Teranga Lions beat Morocco 1-0 in January's final but were stripped of the title in March by a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board, which imposed a 3-0 forfeit after they walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty awarded against them when the game was goalless.

Following a hearing in Lausanne in October, a three-man Cas panel unanimously overturned that ruling by Caf, effectively judging that the decisions taken by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala in restarting the match and playing it to a conclusion were final.

Morocco's football federation (FRMF), however, says it will "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision".

The North Africans could yet take their fight to the Swiss Federal Court.

Those in Senegal have celebrated the return of the title, while several legal experts have backed the Cas verdict.

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling

Senegal's talisman Sadio Mane, who was named player of the tournament at Afcon 2025, said the ruling "fills us with joy".

The 34-year-old former Liverpool man thanked his team-mates and Senegal staff as well as the whole Senegalese nation at home and abroad.

"Your faith in us gave us strength during the most difficult moments. This victory is yours, too," he said in a statement on social media.

Senegal captain Kalidou Koulibaly, who missed the final through injury, echoed that sentiment.

"Some victories are won on the pitch, while others are won in the heart of a people," he said in a post on Facebook.

"Long before this verdict, there was you - your prayers, your flags in the windows, your fervour, and the pride that unites us all: the pride of the people of Teranga."

Pape Gueye, the man who scored the extra-time winner in Rabat, described the Cas decision as "an immense relief".

Both he and Mane had a message of support for Morocco.

"Senegal and Morocco are brotherly nations; may our shared passion for football continue to bring us closer together," Mane said.

Gueye added: "Beyond football, the respect and fraternity between our two peoples remain what matters most. Let's hold on to that.

Morocco's main complaint is that Articles 82 and 84 of Afcon tournament regulations - which were implemented by the Caf appeals board in March - were not followed by Cas.

Article 82 states that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee" it shall be "considered [the loser] and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition".

Article 84 then states a 3-0 forfeit should be imposed on a team which is eliminated in such circumstances.

"There [are] football rules that should have been applied by the referee," former Morocco international Hassan Kachloul told BBC Sport.

"When the Senegalese players left the pitch, the game should have been over."

The FRMF registered its "surprise" at the Cas decision and said that the panel "failed to account for the stance recently established" by the International Football Association Board (Ifab), the game's ultimate lawmakers, and world governing body Fifa regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee's permission.

However, Ifab only updated its laws in April - three months after the Afcon final - to state that a referee may send off any player who leaves the field when protesting a decision.

Moroccan football journalist Jalal Bounouar says his compatriots are "frustrated and disappointed" by the ruling.

"The main reason is that Caf's appeal board had already applied Article 82 and 84 of the competition regulations which considered Senegal to have forfeited the match," he told Newsday on the BBC World Service.

"Many Moroccans feel the decision by Cas has ignored the importance of these rules. From the Moroccan perspective, the referee should have taken stronger disciplinary action.

"We feel that our team was put in a difficult situation and that the final was not managed fairly."

Cas has a long-standing practice of following what has been called the 'field of play' doctrine.

It refrains from "reviewing decisions taken on the playing field by referees for applying the rules of the game, unless there is evidence that those rules were applied arbitrarily or in bad faith".

"The primary argument was that the referee is the master of the decision on the pitch," said Serge Vittoz, a member of the FSF's legal team.

Raymond Hack, both a former head of disciplinary at Caf and a former arbiter at Cas, said the judgement was the "correct verdict".

"What everyone seems to forget - and whilst there may be contradictory information in Article 82 and 84 - decisions taken by the referee during the match are final," the South African told the BBC World Service.

"Only the referee can start a game. Only a referee can end a game."

For former Nigeria striker Daniel Amokachi, an Afcon winner in 1994, the Cas ruling is "the right decision".

"At the end of the day, the man in charge of the match (Ndala) restarted the game, the game ended," he said.

Caf has already tightened its own regulations to avoid a repeat.

But Algerian sports journalist Maher Mezahi says the continental governing body still needs to salvage its image.

"How many times have we seen Caf's legal institutions, whether it be the disciplinary board or the appeals committee, come up with these decisions that we all find ridiculous," he said.

"They end up being challenged at Cas and eventually they get overturned.

"We have to rebuild trust in Caf's own judicial bodies because it is a little bit humiliating and degrading and it brings the entire reputation of the confederation into disrepute."

The 2027 Afcon is scheduled to take place in June and July next year, and Senegal and Morocco were among the first qualifiers earlier this month.

Kachloul says the next tournament provides a chance to draw a definitive line under what happened in Rabat in January.

"This event, wherever you look at it on the Senegalese side or Moroccan side, doesn't look good at all," the one-time Aston Villa midfielder said.

"They are lucky to have another [Afcon] tournament in six months to redeem themselves and to paint a better picture of African football.

"The best way to prove that you're the best is to go back on the pitch and let the football talk."

articles.title: Iñigo: "Nos falta finura y tenemos un componente de ansiedad alto"
articles.standfirst: El técnico no oculta que el equipo tiene carencias, pero espera que este tipo de victorias ayuden a encontrar el camino
articles.summary: El técnico no oculta que el equipo tiene carencias, pero espera que este tipo de victorias ayuden a encontrar el camino
articles.body: El entrenador del Villarreal ha sido el primero en reconocer que el equipo no está bien, pero que logró una victoria que es clave para la temporada europea del equipo. Iñigo espera que sea un punto clave para que el equipo siga creciendo y corrigiendo los errores que sigue mostrando a las puertas de diciembre. Triunfo: "La victoria es fundamental en cuanto a la competición. Los jugadores sienten la responsabilidad con su camiseta, el club, la afición y la ansiedad aparece. El jugador del Villarreal entiende la situación y, en vez de jugar liberado… las victorias generan confianza". Falta de fluidez arriba: "Hay un desconocimiento amplio del equipo al que nos hemos enfrentado. Ellos persiguen al hombre campo a campo, son los que más corren de la competición. Nos falta finura y tenemos un componente de ansiedad alto, pero los jugadores son personas. Hay muchos puntos positivos con el triunfo y ojala estas victorias nos den esa finura". Forma de ganar: "El cómo es muy importante. A largo plazo es donde se consigue el éxito. El compromiso y la actitud son brillantes, pero si encajamos la última falta, diríamos otra cosa. Hay que seguir mejorando". Árbitro: "Nunca hablo de decisiones arbitrales. Es una línea roja que trazo y nunca la rebaso". Luiz Junior: "No hay nada perenne en mis decisiones. Prevalece el día a día. Decido dependiendo del rival y la situación física. Logan, que ha sido el mejor del partido, y Luiz nos han ayudado muchísimo". Logan: "Hay gente con la que, por edad o por lesiones graves, creo que la cocción debe ser más lenta. Logan viene de una lesión grave, pero ha trabajado bien. Todos tendrán opciones si lo siguen demostrando".

articles.title: Lucky break? Bruno Fernandes scores bizarre Man United goal thanks to divot
articles.summary: Fernandes saw his shot take a wicked deflection off the Estadio Jose Alvalade pitch, beating the helpless goalkeeper
articles.body:
Bruno Fernandes scored a bizarre goal for Manchester United against former club Sporting as his long-range shot took a fortuitous bobble off the Estádio José Alvalade pitch.

Moments after the United captain levelled against Sporting from the penalty spot, Fernandes saw his low strike beat goalkeeper Kaique Pereira after what appeared to be a deflection.

But the assist went to a divot in the pitch, as the low left-footed shot from Fernandes struck the turf and diverted away from the stranded goalkeeper Pereira to find the net.

The uneven pitch almost acted as a ramp as the ball suddenly jumped up and flew over Pereira, who was left with no chance.

It was perhaps the lucky break new United manager Mauricio Pochettino needed after a chaotic first half where several decisions went against his team.

It also came after Leny Yoro was ruled to have been wrongly sent off in the eighth minute of United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday in Pochettino's first match.

United's fortunes began to turn after half-time in Lisbon when Lisandro Martinez was fouled and Fernandes stepped up form the spot to equalise.

United captain Fernandes, who played 137 times for Sporting in three seasons in Lisbon, then tried his luck from distance but was rewarded with the deflection.

articles.title: 😳 Bayern star stunned! Mbappé's brother catches FCB on the counter
articles.summary: Now Bayern are stumbling in the Champions League after all! Germany’s record champions are trailing 2-1 at Lille in the closing stages. The Munich side were...
articles.body:
Now Bayern are stumbling in the Champions League after all! Germany's record champions are trailing 2-1 at Lille in the closing stages.

The Munich side were well and truly caught on the counter for the second goal in particular. Ethan Mbappé, the brother of Real Madrid star Kylian, burst forward from his own half. From the halfway line, he had a pretty clear run, with Bayern having pushed too far up the pitch. The attacker raced towards Jonas Urbig but only hit the inside of the left post. Aleksandar Pavlovic rushed back to clear, but in a desperately unlucky turn of events, put the ball into his own net.

The look on his face says it all. A truly bitter evening for Germany's record champions. Can they still turn it around?
